subject: Saturn Edge Collocation — egress bridge & runbook draft
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@saturnsys.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Saturn RFP <rfp@saturnsys.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Oct 2029 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Saturn Edge Collocation — egress bridge & runbook draft

Hi Monica / Jonas,

Thanks again for taking a look. We (Saturn Systems) are exploring a pilot where a small cluster of tenant runtime nodes will be collocated inside our partner colo in Phoenix. Key constraints:

- Outbound egress must go through our perimeter firewall and egress NAT pools (we cannot allow direct public egress from tenant hosts).
- No cross-tenant egress — any caching or shared services must enforce strict network separation.
- We need an operations runbook and a concise architecture sketch to share with our security reviewers (SOC and networking).

Attached is a rough sketch of the deployment (saturn-edge-sketch-v1.pdf). Can Redwood propose an egress bridging pattern that meets the constraints above, and call out where the control plane sits (on-prem vs. remote) and any changes to the KV cache or prefix caching we should expect? Also, can you include a short list of audit evidence items we can present (flow logs, ACLs, cert rotation audit)?

Timing: our internal review is next Friday, so a draft by Wednesday would be ideal.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Engineering Manager, Integrations
Saturn Systems

[attachment: saturn-edge-sketch-v1.pdf]

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@saturnsys.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Oct 2029 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Saturn Edge Collocation — egress bridge & runbook draft

Alex — thanks for the clear constraints and the sketch. We're confident we can propose a pattern that preserves your egress controls and keeps tenant traffic isolated. Initial thoughts (high level):

- Place a lightweight egress-bridge sidecar in the tenant runtime plane that performs NAT to your approved egress CIDRs and enforces per-tenant flow tagging.
- Keep the Redwood control plane in our hosted region (reduces ops burden), but expose a minimal control-plane relay in the colo for ACL provisioning and cert bootstrapping.
- KV cache: run local per-tenant caches in the tenant runtime (no shared KV cluster in colo). If we need a shared cache for efficiency, we will place it behind strict network policies and per-tenant namespaces.

I'll put together a one-page runbook and a diagram set for Wednesday. Questions for you to confirm:
1) Preferred egress source CIDR ranges and any SNAT IPs we must use.
2) Whether the colo will accept our BGP announcements or you require NAT-only egress.
3) Any audit evidence format requirements (CSV vs. syslog ingestion).

Attaching a short list of initial questions for your security team (saturn-initial-questions.md). Will loop in Karthik for any control-plane routing constraints.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Deployments — Redwood Inference

[attachment: saturn-initial-questions.md]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex@saturnsys.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Oct 2029 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Saturn Edge Collocation — egress bridge & runbook draft

On Fri, Oct 11, 2029 at 6:03 PM Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com> wrote:
> I'll put together a one-page runbook and a diagram set for Wednesday.

Looping in some technical detail to include in the diagram and runbook:

- Egress bridge pattern: small per-tenant sidecar (containerized) that intercepts outgoing connections at the node egress layer and forwards via an L3 SNAT gateway owned by Saturn. Sidecar responsibilities: TLS termination for upstream destinations (if required), per-tenant metrics tagging, and health checks.
- Control plane footprint: keep control plane API endpoints in-hosted Redwood; deploy a relay agent in the colo that handles ACL push, cert rotation requests, and local probe aggregation. Relay agent communicates outbound to Redwood control plane over mTLS to avoid inbound rules changes.
- KV cache: enforce strict namespaces; do not run a single shared instance across tenants. If low-latency cache hits are required, we recommend a tiny, local in-memory cache per runtime node.

Operational concerns and action items (for the runbook):
- Flow logs: enable VPC flow logs to a collector we can consume (S3 + CloudTrail-like records) — include expected log fields and retention.
- Fail-open behavior: define whether the sidecar should fail-closed (block outbound) on control-plane loss; recommended default: fail-closed for regulated workloads.
- HA: plan for dual NAT IPs and relay redundancy — provide cutover steps.

I mocked up a concise topology (egress-bridge-proposal.png) showing sidecar -> SATURN-NAT -> Internet and control-plane relay -> hosted-control-plane over mTLS. Suggest we review this in a 30m design call (Jonas/Karthik/Monica + Saturn network/security). I created a Jira ticket for the work: NET-2341.

Jonas Weber
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

[attachment: egress-bridge-proposal.png]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex@saturnsys.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Oct 2029 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Saturn Edge Collocation — egress bridge & runbook draft

Thanks, team — this is the right direction. Quick decisions / asks before Wednesday's draft: 

- Monica: confirm whether Saturn prefers a relay agent in colo (push model) or a purely outbound-only relay that we never accept inbound connections to. My preference is outbound-only mTLS from relay -> hosted-control-plane to simplify their firewall policy.
- Naomi: please run a quick latency and MTU validation plan for the Phoenix colo (we need expected p99 RTT to the hosted control-plane in us-west). Naomi, can you capture baseline traceroutes and a 48-hour measurement?
- Legal / Procurement: ask Saturn for a short colocation addendum that clarifies IP ownership and egress NAT liability — Alex, can you start that conversation and share any template? DocuSign link would be ideal.

Next meeting: propose Wed 2029-10-16 10:00 AM PT for a 30-min design sync. Monica — once you publish the one-pager, I'll add a short decision matrix for HA and fail-open behavior.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Product Operations — Redwood Inference
